queue_items.claim: The row quotes the whole of oshb:Job.6.21 across the verse's ketiv/qere adjacency with no K/Q disclosure, then glosses the quoted string as 'all second-person plural'.
queue_items.grounds: pmarks_Job.json kq registers 1 note at Job.6.21 (book total 53 notes / 49 verses, flagged HIGH), and the staged OSHB extract carries ketiv and qere ADJACENT inside the verse: the spliced pair is לא ל֑וֹ (ketiv unpointed, qere pointed), standing between the 2mp perfect and the 2mp imperfect. The row's quoted run reproduces the entire verse and therefore CROSSES that adjacency -- the canonical disclosure trigger (TOOLKIT wording, re-asserted at strategy §4). The quote is not byte-false (collate.py returns tier byte at oshb:Job.6.21), which is why the omission matters: a doubled reading is presented silently as continuous verse text, and the appended 'all second-person plural' gloss covers a string two of whose words -- the ketiv/qere pair -- are not second-person at all. The verse's three finite verbs ARE 2mp, so the person analysis holds; the defect is the missing K/Q disclosure and the over-wide gloss extent. Not load-bearing: the row's edges rest on 6:14 and 6:24, not on 6:21, and the 6:20|6:21 rival is disclosed either way.
queue_items.proposed_change: Field repair only: inside the oshb:Job.6.21 parenthetical, disclose that the quoted span crosses the verse's ketiv/qere adjacency (WLC single-witness; ketiv and qere adjacent in the extract) and narrow the person gloss to the verse's three finite verbs. Span, edges and the low band unchanged.

trigger_dispositions.grounds: The low band is honest and its stated reason survives re-derivation. Both EDGES stand on tier-1 signals in their own bytes and are argued compatibly by the adjacent units: the near edge on the third-person gnomic turn at oshb:Job.6.14 (collates BYTE; the friend-word carries a 3ms suffix and the verb is 3ms imperfect, and the unit closing at 6:13 names the same seam), the far edge on the imperative opening oshb:Job.6.24 (collates BYTE in the unit beginning there, which argues it as its own near edge). The band is driven by a disclosed INTERNAL rival at 6:20|6:21, and that rival's digit-bearing claim is TRUE on re-derivation: oshb:Job.6.14 through oshb:Job.6.20 carry no second-person form at all, 6:21 supplies the unit's first 2mp verbs, and a 2mp verb or 2mp suffix then stands in every one of the nine verses 6:21, 6:22, 6:23, 6:24, 6:25, 6:26, 6:27, 6:28, 6:29, with oshb:Job.6.30 reverting to 1cs -- so 'runs unbroken through 6:29 (nine verses)' is exact. Span is 10 verses, inside §6's ~4-12 vv guide, crossing no speech boundary. The confidence is not over-stated (no byte-defective warrant is masked) and not materially under-stated (a comparably warranted internal seam is genuinely unresolved). The cross-unit reference is verse-anchored (2:6|2:7), so no register arm attaches.

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: A third-person topic shift opens the row: “To him who is ready to faint, kindness should be shown from his friend; even to him who forsakes the fear of the Almighty.” web:Job.6.14 (Hebrew לַמָּ֣ס מֵרֵעֵ֣הוּ חָ֑סֶד וְיִרְאַ֖ת שַׁדַּ֣י יַעֲזֽוֹב, oshb:Job.6.14, grammatically third-person throughout -- the friend-word carries a 3ms suffix and the verb is 3ms imperfect, with no vocative particle), pivoting the subject-matter from Job's own exhaustion to a gnomic charge against companions in general. He extends the charge with the brook-caravan metaphor, “My brothers have dealt deceitfully as a brook, as the channel of brooks that pass away;” web:Job.6.15, traces the image through the melting ice and vanishing caravans of web:Job.6.16-Job.6.20, then the address itself turns second-person for the first time in the unit, “For now you are nothing. You see a terror, and are afraid.” web:Job.6.21 (Hebrew כִּֽי עַ֭תָּה הֱיִ֣יתֶם לא ל֑וֹ תִּֽרְא֥וּ חֲ֝תַ֗ת וַתִּירָֽאוּ, oshb:Job.6.21, all second-person plural), before closing on a pair of denials that he ever asked the friends for a gift or ransom, web:Job.6.22-Job.6.23. This second-person address shift at 6:21 is a genuine tier-1 signal, not mere texture; it runs unbroken to the end of the chapter, and it is disclosed here as a live internal candidate for this unit's own seam rather than dismissed. It is not adopted as the row's own edge because the third-person charge and its direct application are held together as one movement of the friend-rebuke closing on Job's self-examination through 6:23; the alternative seam at 6:20|6:21 is disclosed here as a live, comparably warranted rival rather than resolved.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Breaking the row at Job.6.20|Job.6.21 for the second-person turn there is a live rival, not a texture-only consideration: 6:21 opens the unit's first 2mp forms and second-person address runs unbroken through 6:29 (nine verses, Job.6.21-Job.6.29), a comparably or better-warranted internal seam than the 6:23|6:24 edge kept here. It is disclosed rather than adopted because the row is held as one continuous rebuke of the friends across the third-person charge and its direct application; the question is left open rather than resolved, in the same spirit as the frame's own disclosed 2:6|2:7 crux.
shipped_row.literature_type_guess: friends rebuke: why abandon one brought low and helpless

prev_row.boundary_rationale: A topic-turn interrogative-wish opens the row: מִֽי יִ֭תֵּן תָּב֣וֹא שֶֽׁאֱלָתִ֑י וְ֝תִקְוָתִ֗י יִתֵּ֥ן אֱלֽוֹהַּ (oshb:Job.6.8), an instance of the dialogue-wide mi-yitten wish formula (sweep: 9 verses book-wide, 10 tokens, one verse carrying two, independently re-swept at skeleton tier). Job spells the wish out as a plea to be let go and cut off web:Job.6.9, holds his one consolation to be that he has “not denied the words of the Holy One” web:Job.6.10, then turns to a run of rhetorical questions about his exhausted capacity, “What is my strength, that I should wait? What is my end, that I should be patient?” web:Job.6.11, “Is my strength the strength of stones? Or is my flesh of bronze?” web:Job.6.12, closing on the admission that “wisdom is driven away from me” web:Job.6.13. The row ends before the next strophe's turn from Job's own exhausted capacity to a third-person accusation of the friends, opening at Job.6.14.
prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending the row through Job.6.14 would merge the wish-formula lament with the brook-metaphor rebuke of the friends that follows it.
prev_row.literature_type_guess: death wish strophe: Job seeks release from torment

next_row.boundary_rationale: An imperative shift opens the row: ה֭וֹרוּנִי וַאֲנִ֣י אַחֲרִ֑ישׁ וּמַה שָּׁ֝גִ֗יתִי הָבִ֥ינוּ לִֽי (oshb:Job.6.24), Job's invitation to be corrected rather than the denial he had just voiced. He weighs “words of uprightness” against the friends' empty reproof web:Job.6.25, protests that their reproof treats the speeches of one who is desperate as mere wind while they would gamble away the fatherless web:Job.6.26-Job.6.27, then appeals directly, “Now therefore be pleased to look at me, for surely I will not lie to your face.” web:Job.6.28, repeats the appeal, “Please return. Let there be no injustice. Yes, return again. My cause is righteous.” web:Job.6.29, and closes on a self-examining question, “Is there injustice on my tongue? Can’t my taste discern mischievous things?” web:Job.6.30. The row runs from the imperative petition to the end of the chapter, closing Job's rebuke of the friends before the reply turns, in the next chapter, to a meditation on human toil in general.
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Carrying the row back to include the brook-metaphor rebuke above it would stretch one strophe well past a comfortable length without an intervening tier-1 seam to justify the span. A second rival was weighed at this row's own near edge: 6:28 opens with the ve'attah turn, וְ֭עַתָּה הוֹאִ֣ילוּ פְנוּ בִ֑י וְעַל פְּ֝נֵיכֶ֗ם אִם אֲכַזֵּֽב (oshb:Job.6.28) -- a device that sweeps 8 book-wide (Job.6.28, Job.30.1, Job.30.9, Job.30.16, Job.35.15, Job.37.21, Job.42.5, Job.42.8) and keys strophe structure elsewhere in the book -- followed at 6:29 by an imperative-plus-na, שֻֽׁבוּ נָ֭א אַל תְּהִ֣י עַוְלָ֑ה ושבי וְשׁ֥וּבוּ ע֝וֹד צִדְקִי בָֽהּ (oshb:Job.6.29), the same form-class opening 5:1 (קְֽרָא נָ֭א) and 4:7 (זְכָר נָ֗א). Splitting at 6:27|6:28 was rejected because 6:28's appeal ('look at me... I will not lie to your face') and 6:29's renewed imperative ('return... my cause is righteous') both continue rather than reopen the direct appeal Job begins at 6:24 -- one imperative-headed appeal running from ה֭וֹרוּנִי at 6:24 through the self-examining close at 6:30 -- so the row is kept whole through both internal signals rather than split at either.
next_row.literature_type_guess: Job appeals: teach me what error caused this punishment

queue_items.claim: The rejected alternative is rejected solely on a strophe-length ground that is off-band against the book's own guide and is ruled non-evidence by the book's own granularity policy.
queue_items.grounds: Arithmetic: the merge the row rejects is Job.7.11-Job.7.21 = 11 verses (6 + 5), INSIDE strategy §6's stated '~4-12 vv guide' for a strophe-level row, so 'past a comfortable strophe length' is false against the book's own band. §6 further rules row comparability a 'convergence constraint, not evidence', so length cannot carry a rival's rejection at all. The sound ground was already in hand and is stated in the row's own boundary_rationale: the verse-initial topic-turn interrogative opening oshb:Job.7.17 (collates BYTE at its cited ref), a tier-1 class in §6's list, which the preceding unit independently names as the edge it stops before. The seam therefore stands; what fails is the rival's stated rejection ground.
queue_items.proposed_change: Field repair only: re-ground the rejection on the tier-1 topic-turn interrogative opening Job.7.17 (oshb:Job.7.17 is already in the refs) and delete the strophe-length assertion. No span change.

queue_items.claim: literature_type_guess describes material that stands nowhere in the row's span.
queue_items.grounds: The shipped label is 'divine arbitration impossibility: no umpire between Job and God'. A web-phrase sweep for 'umpire' over WEB Job returns 1 verse book-wide: Job.9.33 -- outside this span, outside chapter 7 and outside this speech (the arbitration material is web:Job.9.32-Job.9.33, inside Job's reply to Bildad). WEB Job.7.17-Job.7.21, which the row itself quotes verbatim, runs the what-is-man interrogative, the every-morning visitation and testing, the how-long plea, the watcher-of-men mark-and-burden accusation, and the closing pardon question: an address to God about divine scrutiny and pardon, with no arbiter, umpire or mediator in it. The label is byte-false for the span. It bears on neither edge, and the row's mark citations are sound -- pmarks_Job.json gives paseq 1 at Job.7.20 and both PE and paseq 1 at Job.7.21, cited from the inventory with no intra-verse position claim and correctly labelled single-witness and corroborating rather than driving.
queue_items.proposed_change: Field repair only: replace literature_type_guess with a label drawn from the span, e.g. 'closing plea: divine scrutiny of man and the unanswered request for pardon'. No span, ref or confidence change.

trigger_dispositions.grounds: 'Merging Job.7.17-21 into the row above it' is a positional row reference: §10's register purge bars process language in row prose and requires cross-row references to be verse-anchored. TEST 2: the reference carries no byte claim about the neighbouring unit, and its substance is verse-anchored elsewhere in the same sentence (Job.7.11, with web:Job.7.11 in boundary_evidence_refs), so the register arm alone is cosmetic and scores low. The argumentative ground that sentence DOES carry is defective on separate grounds and is recorded as its own finding.

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: A topic-turn interrogative opens the row's final movement: מָֽה אֱ֭נוֹשׁ כִּ֣י תְגַדְּלֶ֑נּוּ וְכִי תָשִׁ֖ית אֵלָ֣יו לִבֶּֽךָ (oshb:Job.7.17), “What is man, that you should magnify him, that you should set your mind on him,” web:Job.7.17, continuing the direct address to God with the daily scrutiny of web:Job.7.18, the plea “How long will you not look away from me” web:Job.7.19, and the accusation of being made a “mark” and a “burden” web:Job.7.20 -- a verse that itself carries a paseq segment, tier-3 and single-witness -- closing the speech on “Why do you not pardon my disobedience, and take away my iniquity? For now will I lie down in the dust. You will seek me diligently, but I will not be.” web:Job.7.21. That closing verse also carries a petuchah notation and a paseq segment, both single-witness and both tier-3 at most, corroborating rather than driving the close of the reply here.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging Job.7.17-21 into the row above it would run the Job.7.11 resolve's aftermath and the closing interrogative movement together past a comfortable strophe length.
shipped_row.literature_type_guess: divine arbitration impossibility: no umpire between Job and God

prev_row.boundary_rationale: An emphatic self-reference opens a new resolve: גַּם אֲנִי֮ לֹ֤א אֶחֱשָׂ֫ךְ פִּ֥י אֲֽ֭דַבְּרָה בְּצַ֣ר רוּחִ֑י אָ֝שִׂ֗יחָה בְּמַ֣ר נַפְשִֽׁי (oshb:Job.7.11), “Therefore I will not keep silent. I will speak in the anguish of my spirit. I will complain in the bitterness of my soul.” web:Job.7.11. Job asks “Am I a sea, or a sea monster, that you put a guard over me?” web:Job.7.12, describes a bed that fails to comfort him because God frightens him with dreams web:Job.7.13-Job.7.14, and concludes that his soul “chooses strangling, death rather than my bones” web:Job.7.15, then states outright, “I loathe my life. I don’t want to live forever. Leave me alone, for my days are but a breath.” web:Job.7.16. The row runs from the fronted-pronoun resolve to the loathing-of-life statement it produces, ending before the next topic-turn interrogative.
prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Ending the row at Job.7.10 would cut the fronted-pronoun resolve of Job.7.11 away from the dream-terror and life-loathing material it introduces.
prev_row.literature_type_guess: mortality complaint: days flee like fleeting wind patterns

next_row.boundary_rationale: The verse-initial formula וַ֭יַּעַן בִּלְדַּ֥ד הַשּׁוּחִ֗י וַיֹאמַֽר (oshb:Job.8.1) hands the speech to Bildad; the WEB rendering is “Then Bildad the Shuhite answered,” web:Job.8.1. Bildad's vaya'an-formula family sums to three speeches book-wide across two gentilic spellings, named per member: the plene הַשּׁוּחִ֗י opening this verse (byte tier; the plene spelling itself sweeps 3 book-wide at 2:11, 8:1, 42:9, but only 8:1 is a formula opening), and the defective הַשֻּׁחִ֗י opening his later two speeches, oshb:Job.18.1 and oshb:Job.25.1 (byte tier; sweeps 2 book-wide). The family total of three formula members is a sum across these two named spellings, not one blended string. Bildad rebukes Job's outburst, “How long will you speak these things? Shall the words of your mouth be a mighty wind?” web:Job.8.2, states his retribution doctrine as a rhetorical denial, “Does God pervert justice? Or does the Almighty pervert righteousness?” web:Job.8.3, applies it to Job's dead children web:Job.8.4, and offers the conditional promise that follows from the doctrine, “If you want to seek God diligently, make your supplication to the Almighty.” web:Job.8.5, “If you were pure and upright, surely now he would awaken for you, and make the habitation of your righteousness prosperous.” web:Job.8.6, closing on the promise that “your latter end would greatly increase” web:Job.8.7. The row runs from the speech formula through the doctrine's opening statement, ending before Bildad turns to an appeal to ancestral precedent.
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Isolating Job.8.1 as its own row would separate Bildad's formula from the doctrine it introduces without a competing tier-1 signal before the imperative appeal to precedent that follows.
next_row.literature_type_guess: Bildad opens: ancient wisdom on retribution doctrine

queue_items.claim: The row's 'repeats -- at byte tier --' for the tam bond is byte-false: the 9:22 token matches 9:20/9:21 only at skeleton tier.
queue_items.grounds: Spliced from verse_map_oshb.json: oshb:Job.9.22 word 6 reads תָּ֥ם (qamats + MERKHA U+05A5), while oshb:Job.9.20 word 5 and oshb:Job.9.21 word 1 both read תָּֽם (qamats + METEG U+05BD). collate_hebrew of the 9:22 token against the 9:20 window returns tier 'skeleton', not 'byte'; accent_stripped also fails because the Job extract RETAINS meteg (TOOLKIT_AUDIT encoding note). The two preceding tokens ARE byte-identical to each other (collate of the 9:20 token against the 9:21 window returns 'byte'), which is what makes the 'twice' half of the sentence true and the tier label the only false part. The row's own prose displays the two distinct pointed forms while asserting byte identity between them.
queue_items.proposed_change: In boundary_rationale replace 'repeats - at byte tier - the word' with 'repeats at SKELETON tier (distinct pointed forms: merkha at 9:22, meteg at 9:20 and 9:21, which are byte-identical to each other) the word'.

queue_items.claim: The splice-plus-gloss 'Job.9.23's NEQIYIM (mocks)' names the wrong word: the token glossed is the plural noun 'innocent ones', not the mocking verb the argument needs.
queue_items.grounds: oshb:Job.9.23 reads (word order) ... לְמַסַּ֖ת / נְקִיִּ֣ם / יִלְעָֽג. The spliced token נְקִיִּ֣ם is the masculine plural of naqi, 'innocent (ones)', standing as the nomen rectum after the construct לְמַסַּ֖ת ('at the trial of'); WEB 9:23 renders it 'the innocent' ('If the scourge kills suddenly, he will mock at the trial of the innocent.'). The subjectless 3ms verb the claim actually depends on is יִלְעָֽג ('he will mock'), the verse's final word. The syntactic observation ('no expressed subject of its own') is true of that verb and cannot be true of a noun in a construct chain, so the warrant survives with the right token; the cited token and gloss do not. Byte-valid splice, semantically wrong word for the claim.
queue_items.proposed_change: In boundary_rationale swap the splice and gloss to the verse-final verb of oshb:Job.9.23, יִלְעָֽג ('he will mock'), re-spliced from verse_map_oshb.json; the surrounding sentence otherwise stands.

trigger_dispositions.grounds: Band honestly reasoned and supported by the row's own evidence. Near edge: the inferential/quotative frame stands in 9:22's own bytes, oshb:Job.9.22 opening אַחַ֗ת הִ֥יא עַל כֵּ֥ן אָמַ֑רְתִּי ('it is all one; therefore I said'), a tier-1 discourse frame introducing the quoted indictment (strategy Job.md 2a/6; WEB 9:22 'It is all the same. Therefore I say he destroys the blameless and the wicked.'). Far edge: the fronted possessive subject at oshb:Job.9.25, וְיָמַ֣י קַ֭לּוּ, is a tier-1 topic/participant turn, and next_row M8-Job-037 argues that same edge identically; prev_row M8-Job-035 closes at 9:21 'before the inferential turn of Job.9.22', so both edges are argued compatibly. The low band is earned by a real counter-pull the row itself discloses (the cross-seam tam bond, 9:20/9:21 vs 9:22) and by the 9:22|9:23 subject question; it is neither over-stated (no seam rests on a defective warrant) nor under-stated (a merge into the courtroom strophe remains genuinely arguable). No parashah mark and no K/Q sits in 9:22-9:24 (pmarks_Job.json marks {} for ch.9, kq {} in span; the paseq at Job.9.24 is count-only and the row makes no mark claim). Calibration clean; the row's separate findings below are field-level, not band-level.

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: An explicit quotative frame opens this short strophe: אַחַ֗ת הִ֥יא עַל כֵּ֥ן (glossed ‘it is all one; therefore I say’, Job.9.22), introducing the indictment “he destroys the blameless and the wicked” web:Job.9.22. This opening word, תָּ֥ם (‘blameless’), repeats — at byte tier — the word that twice closes the preceding strophe's argument (תָּֽם at Job.9.20 word 5, תָּֽם at Job.9.21 word 1), a cross-seam lexical bond disclosed here rather than left implicit; it corroborates continuity of the courtroom-to-indictment argument across 9.21|9.22 without moving either strophe's edge. Job.9.23-Job.9.24 extend the same indictment: Job.9.22's מְכַלֶּֽה (‘destroys’) carries an explicit third-person subject, ה֣וּא, and Job.9.23's נְקִיִּ֣ם (‘mocks’) has no expressed subject of its own — WEB's own rendering keeps the pronoun 'he' across the verse boundary rather than naming 'the scourge' as a fresh subject, so the mocking agent is left as open a question in the Hebrew as in English; either way the indictment stays continuous, reaching “The earth is given into the hand of the wicked” web:Job.9.24, closing on the rhetorical question “If not he, then who is it?” web:Job.9.24. The subject shifts from this cosmic indictment to Job's own fleeting days at Job.9.25, marking the strophe's far edge.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding Job.9.22-Job.9.24 into the preceding courtroom-inability argument was rejected given the explicit inferential frame that opens Job.9.22 and the fresh third-person subject (earth, judges) it introduces.
shipped_row.literature_type_guess: theodicy indictment: God mocks the calamity of innocent

prev_row.boundary_rationale: An a-fortiori particle opens the strophe: אַ֭ף כִּֽי (glossed ‘how much less’, Job.9.14), drawing the direct implication from the preceding power-hymn that Job himself cannot answer God. A chain of אם-protases follows (Job.9.15-Job.9.16, Job.9.19-Job.9.20) arguing that no hearing could be fair even for an innocent man: “Though I am righteous, my own mouth will condemn me” web:Job.9.20. The strophe closes on the bare declarative תָּֽם אָ֭נִי (“I am blameless. I don't respect myself. I despise my life.” web:Job.9.21), a personal verdict that ends the courtroom-inability argument before the inferential turn of Job.9.22.
prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Closing this strophe at Job.9.20 was rejected because Job.9.21's self-verdict completes the courtroom argument's clause chain rather than opening an unrelated one.
prev_row.literature_type_guess: complaint of innocence: all alike perish by divine hand

next_row.boundary_rationale: The fronted possessive subject וְיָמַ֣י קַ֭לּוּ (“Now my days are swifter than a runner” web:Job.9.25) turns the topic from the theodicy indictment to Job's own vanishing lifespan, using simile (“as the swift ships, as the eagle that swoops on the prey” web:Job.9.26). A pair of אם-protases then brackets the futility of self-vindication: Job.9.27 ( “I will forget my complaint” web:Job.9.27 ) and Job.9.30 ( washing with snow ), both resolving to the same fear ( “I know that you will not hold me innocent” web:Job.9.28 ) and closing on “My own clothes will abhor me” web:Job.9.31, before the כי-clause of Job.9.32 reopens the courtroom register directly.
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: A break at Job.9.27|Job.9.28 was considered but rejected since the paired אם-protases of Job.9.27 and Job.9.30 frame one continuous argument about the futility of self-cleansing.
next_row.literature_type_guess: fleeting days complaint: life flies like courier and shuttle

queue_items.claim: The row mislocates its cross-row comparison: Job.16.12 is the fourth verse of the preceding row, not that row's opening.
queue_items.grounds: Shipped prev row M8-Job-063 span = Job.16.9-Job.16.14. Its opening verse MT Job.16.9 begins אַפּ֤וֹ טָרַ֨ף - itself a subject fronted before its verb - so the comparison the row wants is available at the true opening and the underlying point (fronting is ambient here, hence non-distinctive as an edge signal) survives. What is false is only the locator: שָׁ֘לֵ֤ו הָיִ֨יתִי is byte-exact at oshb:Job.16.12 (byte tier, sole book-wide hit) and Job.16.12 is verse four of the preceding row's six. The same verse also softens the row's other contrast, between 'the described object of a third-person assault (Job.16.9-Job.16.14)' and 'the grammatical subject of his own 1cs acts': הָיִ֨יתִי at oshb:Job.16.12 is itself a 1cs qatal inside the range said to hold Job as object.
queue_items.proposed_change: PROPOSAL ONLY (field repair, no span change): re-word to 'the preceding row's own opening also fronts a term before its verb (אַפּ֤וֹ טָרַ֨ף, oshb:Job.16.9), as does Job.16.12 inside it', and add oshb:Job.16.9 to boundary_evidence_refs.

trigger_dispositions.grounds: Calibration is sound at medium_low. The seam at Job.16.14|Job.16.15 is a real participant-role shift standing in the cited verse's own bytes: MT Job.16.15 opens שַׂ֣ק תָּ֭פַרְתִּי (fronted object plus 1cs qatal) and continues 1cs at וְעֹלַ֖לְתִּי, against MT Job.16.9-Job.16.14 where the assailant is subject and Job the object (אַפּ֤וֹ טָרַ֨ף וַֽיִּשְׂטְמֵ֗נִי at oshb:Job.16.9). But the seam carries no formula, no vocative and no parashah mark (pmarks_Job.json records no PE/SAMEKH anywhere in ch 16 - absence is never counterevidence, only the absence of corroboration), and the role contrast is not clean, since MT Job.16.12 already opens on a 1cs subject clause שָׁ֘לֵ֤ו הָיִ֨יתִי inside the preceding row. The row itself concedes the softness ('word order alone does not distinguish this row's edge'). No Job cap is implicated: this is a 3-verse in-speech strophe row, not a whole chapter. Confidence is neither over- nor under-stated.

Two positional row references in the driver field, and the first carries a byte-FALSE claim about another row, so the E-18 arm applies and the disposition is medium, not cosmetic. 'The preceding row's own opening also fronts a term before its verb (שָׁ֘לֵ֤ו הָיִ֨יתִי, ... Job.16.12)': the preceding row M8-Job-063 spans Job.16.9-Job.16.14, so its OPENING verse is Job.16.9, whose own first words are אַפּ֤וֹ טָרַ֨ף (subject before verb); שָׁ֘לֵ֤ו הָיִ֨יתִי (byte tier at oshb:Job.16.12) stands at the FOURTH verse of that row. The second reference ('a short unit that ends before the vocative apostrophe to the earth opens the next row') is TRUE - MT Job.16.18 opens on the vocative אֶ֭רֶץ - but is anchored to no ref at all: neither web:Job.16.18 nor oshb:Job.16.18 appears in boundary_evidence_refs.

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: Job turns from describing the assault to his own response to it, fronting the object of his mourning ritual: שַׂ֣ק תָּ֭פַרְתִּי עֲלֵ֣י גִלְדִּ֑י, “I have sewed sackcloth on my skin, and have thrust my horn in the dust.” (web:Job.16.15), continued in his physical distress, “My face is red with weeping. Deep darkness is on my eyelids,” (web:Job.16.16), and closing on a protest of innocence, “although there is no violence in my hands, and my prayer is pure.” (web:Job.16.17). The preceding row's own opening also fronts a term before its verb (שָׁ֘לֵ֤ו הָיִ֨יתִי, 'I was at ease,' Job.16.12), so word order alone does not distinguish this row's edge; what changes at Job.16.15 is Job's grammatical role, from the described object of a third-person assault (Job.16.9-Job.16.14) to the grammatical subject of his own 1cs acts (שַׂ֣ק תָּ֭פַרְתִּי, 'I have sewed') — a participant-role shift, not the fronting by itself, marks the topic turn to Job's own mourning and innocence, a short unit that ends before the vocative apostrophe to the earth opens the next row.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading 16:15-17 as a continuation of the assault sequence would miss the fronted object that marks Job's own response as a new topic.
shipped_row.literature_type_guess: Weeping into dust with face-transformation imagery

prev_row.boundary_rationale: The row shifts from direct second-person address to third-person description of an assailant, “He has torn me in his wrath and persecuted me. He has gnashed on me with his teeth. My adversary sharpens his eyes on me.” (web:Job.16.9), through the crowd's mockery, “They have gaped on me with their mouth. They have struck me on the cheek reproachfully. They gather themselves together against me.” (web:Job.16.10), and the accusation against God directly, “God delivers me to the ungodly, and casts me into the hands of the wicked.” (web:Job.16.11), to a run of violent images closing on “He breaks me with breach on breach. He runs at me like a giant.” (web:Job.16.14). This third-person description of assault is a distinct register from both the retort to the friends and the singular address that precede it, and it gives way to Job's own self-description of mourning at 16:15.
prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging this assault sequence with the mourning-ritual verses that follow would blend third-person description of what has been done to Job with his own direct response to it.
prev_row.literature_type_guess: Divine violence account personified assault metaphor

next_row.boundary_rationale: A vocative apostrophe opens the row, אֶ֭רֶץ אַל תְּכַסִּ֣י דָמִ֑י וְֽאַל יְהִ֥י מָ֝ק֗וֹם לְזַעֲקָתִֽי (oshb:Job.16.18) (“Earth, don't cover my blood. Let my cry have no place to rest.” (web:Job.16.18)), addressing the ground itself rather than the friends or the divine. The row continues on a 'behold'-headed clause, “Even now, behold, my witness is in heaven. He who vouches for me is on high.” (web:Job.16.19), through the friends' scorn, “My friends scoff at me. My eyes pour out tears to God,” (web:Job.16.20), the appeal itself, “that he would maintain the right of a man with God, of a son of man with his neighbor!” (web:Job.16.21), and closes on the approach of death: כִּֽי שְׁנ֣וֹת מִסְפָּ֣ר יֶאֱתָ֑יוּ וְאֹ֖רַח לֹא אָשׁ֣וּב אֶהֱלֹֽךְ (“For when a few years have come, I will go the way of no return.” web:Job.16.22), a ki-headed clause carrying its own finite verb pair. The next verse opens a new, asyndetic clause with a fresh subject and predicate sharing no verb with 16:22 — רוּחִ֣י חֻ֭בָּלָה יָמַ֥י נִזְעָ֗כוּ קְבָרִ֥ים לִֽי (“My spirit is consumed. My days are extinct and the grave is ready for me.” web:Job.17.1). The row crosses the chapter number on topic and address continuity alone: both verses share one mortality theme and no new addressee, formula, or particle intervenes between them, even though they are two grammatically separate clauses rather than one continuous sentence; the next shift comes at 17:2's oath-headed turn to the mockers.
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Breaking this row at the chapter number between 16:22 and 17:1 would impose a metadata division at a point where topic and address run unbroken, even though the two verses are grammatically distinct clauses (16:22 ki-headed with its own verb pair; 17:1 asyndetic with a fresh subject and predicate) rather than one continuous sentence.
next_row.literature_type_guess: Blood-crying witness and advocate-seeking legal formulation

queue_items.claim: The opening-seam sentence mis-notates the seam (Job.21.1|Job.22.1 for Job.21.34|Job.22.1) and mis-describes the previous row as closing with the vaya'an of Job.21.1.
queue_items.grounds: Prev row M8-Job-088 span = Job.21.27-Job.21.34; MT Job.21.1 (וַיַּ֥עַן אִיּ֗וֹב וַיֹּאמַֽר, byte tier, one of the nine book-wide members of the generic Job-reply formula) sits 26 verses before that row's first verse and opens Job's speech, not any row's close. The corpus uses X|Y for ADJACENT verses - this same slice writes 'Job.22.25|Job.22.26' and 'Job.22.24|Job.22.25' - so 'Job.21.1|Job.22.1' is a wrong-seam cite. The seam itself is unaffected and correct: MT Job.22.1 carries the speaker-change formula וַ֭יַּעַן אֱלִיפַ֥ז הַֽתֵּמָנִ֗י וַיֹּאמַֽר (byte tier at oshb:Job.22.1, sole book-wide hit), and the prev row independently corroborates its own close with the SAMEKH after Job.21.34.
queue_items.proposed_change: PROPOSAL ONLY (field repair, no span change): 'The speaker-change seam at Job.21.34|Job.22.1 opens this row: Job's speech, opened by וַיַּ֥עַן אִיּ֗וֹב וַיֹּאמַֽר at oshb:Job.21.1, ends at Job.21.34, and this row opens with Eliphaz answering, וַ֭יַּעַן אֱלִיפַ֥ז הַֽתֵּמָנִ֗י וַיֹּאמַֽר (oshb:Job.22.1)'.

queue_items.claim: 'Eliphaz's fifth and final ha-interrogative in this speech falls outside this row, at Job.22.12' is byte-false as to 'final': a sixth verse-initial interrogative he opens Job.22.15.
queue_items.grounds: Re-swept over the first word of every verse of Eliphaz's third speech (MT Job.22.2-Job.22.30) in verse_map_oshb.json. Verse-initial interrogative he: Job.22.2 הַלְאֵ֥ל, Job.22.3 הַחֵ֣פֶץ, Job.22.4 הֲֽ֭מִיִּרְאָ֣תְךָ, Job.22.5 הֲלֹ֣א, Job.22.12 הֲֽלֹא and Job.22.15 הַאֹ֣רַח - six members, so Job.22.12 is correctly the FIFTH but is not the final one. WEB Job.22.15 confirms the interrogative reading ('Will you keep the old way, which wicked men have trodden,'), the question running on into Job.22.16 so that no question mark falls inside Job.22.15 itself. The two near-miss verse-initial he-tokens are correctly excluded from the series: Job.22.17's הָאֹמְרִ֣ים is the qamats-he ARTICLE on a participle and Job.22.21's הַסְכֶּן is a hiphil imperative. Not load-bearing - the claim sits beyond the row's far edge and neither the seam nor the rival's rejection rests on it. (The row's other digits in this field re-derive TRUE: the defective Temanite spelling sweeps 1 book-wide, at Job.22.1 alone, and the fuller spelling 5 book-wide at Job.2.11, Job.4.1, Job.15.1, Job.42.7 and Job.42.9, exactly the members listed - a spelling-level, not byte-level, object, the pointed form הַֽתֵּמָנִ֗י at oshb:Job.22.1 being a byte singleton and הַֽתֵּימָנִ֗י standing byte-identically at oshb:Job.4.1 and oshb:Job.15.1 only.)
queue_items.proposed_change: PROPOSAL ONLY (field repair, no span change): 'Eliphaz's fifth ha-interrogative falls outside this row at Job.22.12, and a sixth and final one opens Job.22.15 (הַאֹ֣רַח, oshb:Job.22.15).'

trigger_dispositions.grounds: The matched clause - 'the first three of which WEB's own punctuation further unpacks into four question-marked clauses, since Job.22.3's second colon (וְאִם בֶּ֝֗צַע כִּֽי תַתֵּ֥ם דְּרָכֶֽיךָ) is also rendered as a question though it opens on a mid-verse וְאִם rather than a fresh he-token' - is a translation-punctuation fact sitting in the driver field with no tier-4 disclosure, and it carries argumentative weight: it amplifies the interrogative-density characterization of Job.22.2-Job.22.5 on which the far-edge rejection at Job.22.5|Job.22.6 leans. It is factually TRUE (WEB Job.22.2 carries one question mark, WEB Job.22.3 two, WEB Job.22.4 one = four question-marked clauses out of the first three he-tokens; the second colon does open mid-verse on וְאִם), and web:Job.22.2, web:Job.22.3, web:Job.22.4 stand in boundary_evidence_refs. Under the campaign-wide addendum WEB punctuation is tier-4 and is never boundary evidence, so the corroborative use is a defect; severity is LOW because it is a stray remark inside an otherwise byte-grounded case - the opening seam rests on the speaker-change formula וַ֭יַּעַן אֱלִיפַ֥ז הַֽתֵּמָנִ֗י וַיֹּאמַֽר at oshb:Job.22.1 and the far-edge rejection rests separately on the Hebrew הֲלֹ֣א cited as oshb:Job.22.5 and on the connectives of Job.22.6, Job.22.8 and Job.22.11.

'the previous row closes with Job answering (וַיַּ֥עַן אִיּ֗וֹב וַיֹּאמַֽר, oshb:Job.21.1)' is a positional row reference AND is byte-false about that row, so the E-18 arm applies at medium: shipped prev row M8-Job-088 spans Job.21.27-Job.21.34 and closes at Job.21.34 (pmarks_Job.json: marks[Job.21.34] = SAMEKH, which that row itself cites), so וַיַּ֥עַן אִיּ֗וֹב וַיֹּאמַֽר at MT Job.21.1 is the previous SPEECH's opening formula, not the previous ROW's close. The same sentence also mis-notates the seam as 'Job.21.1|Job.22.1', pairing two verses 34 apart in the corpus's own adjacent-verse pipe notation; the actual seam is Job.21.34|Job.22.1.

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: The speaker-change seam at Job.21.1|Job.22.1 opens this row: the previous row closes with Job answering (וַיַּ֥עַן אִיּ֗וֹב וַיֹּאמַֽר, oshb:Job.21.1), and this row opens with Eliphaz answering instead (וַ֭יַּעַן אֱלִיפַ֥ז הַֽתֵּמָנִ֗י וַיֹּאמַֽר, oshb:Job.22.1; “Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered,” web:Job.22.1). The formula's epithet is spelled defectively here (הַֽתֵּמָנִ֗י) against the fuller spelling Eliphaz's first two formula instances carry (הַֽתֵּימָנִ֗י, oshb:Job.4.1 and oshb:Job.15.1); swept independently, the defective spelling occurs at Job.22.1 alone (sweep: 1 book-wide) while the fuller spelling occurs 5 times book-wide, both in formula position and in narration (oshb:Job.2.11, oshb:Job.4.1, oshb:Job.15.1, oshb:Job.42.7, oshb:Job.42.9). Four verse-initial ha-interrogative tokens open this row in sequence — הַלְאֵ֥ל (Job.22.2), הַחֵ֣פֶץ (Job.22.3), הֲֽ֭מִיִּרְאָ֣תְךָ (Job.22.4), הֲלֹ֣א (Job.22.5) — the first three of which WEB's own punctuation further unpacks into four question-marked clauses, since Job.22.3's second colon (וְאִם בֶּ֝֗צַע כִּֽי תַתֵּ֥ם דְּרָכֶֽיךָ) is also rendered as a question though it opens on a mid-verse וְאִם rather than a fresh he-token; Job.22.5's הֲלֹ֣א (oshb:Job.22.5) sharpens the charge from piety to outright wickedness, setting up the itemized list that follows without yet stating it. Eliphaz's fifth and final ha-interrogative in this speech falls outside this row, at Job.22.12.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Ending the row at Job.22.4 and treating Job.22.5 as an opening line of the accusation catalogue was rejected, since Job.22.5 is still framed as an interrogative continuing the ha-prefixed question series of Job.22.2-Job.22.4, against the declarative register the catalogue itself uses from Job.22.6 on — a register contrast, not an asyndetic one: three of the catalogue's six verses (Job.22.6, Job.22.8, Job.22.11) open on overt connectives (כִּֽי, וְאִ֣ישׁ, אוֹ) rather than asyndetically, Job.22.6 itself a subordinating ki-clause.
shipped_row.literature_type_guess: Eliphaz's third-cycle response opening with piety-premise

prev_row.boundary_rationale: Direct address returns to close the chapter: הֵ֣ן יָ֭דַעְתִּי מַחְשְׁבֽוֹתֵיכֶ֑ם וּ֝מְזִמּ֗וֹת עָלַ֥י תַּחְמֹֽסוּ “Behold, I know your thoughts, the plans with which you would wrong me.” web:Job.21.27, answering the claim Job puts in the friends' own mouths — “Where is the house of the prince?” web:Job.21.28 — with an appeal to travelers' testimony (21:29) that the wicked man is spared for the day of calamity (21:30) and even honored at burial: וְ֭הוּא לִקְבָר֣וֹת יוּבָ֑ל “Yet he will be borne to the grave.” web:Job.21.32. The chapter closes on the same root with which it opened — וְ֭אֵיךְ תְּנַחֲמ֣וּנִי הָ֑בֶל “So how can you comfort me with nonsense” web:Job.21.34 answers “Let this be your consolation.” web:Job.21.2, תְּנַחֲמ֣וּנִי echoing תַּנְח֥וּמֹֽתֵיכֶֽם — turning the friends' own opening request back on them as a rebuke. A SAMEKH follows 21:34 (oshb:Job.21.34 (setumah, single-witness)), corroborating the close of Job's reply immediately before Eliphaz's third-speech formula opens at 22:1.
prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting off 21:32-34 as its own decision would separate the burial-honor image from the accusation it is answering.

next_row.boundary_rationale: The itemized accusation opens with an asyndetic ki-clause, כִּֽי (oshb:Job.22.6, “For you have taken pledges from your brother for nothing” web:Job.22.6), listing specific social wrongs charged directly against the addressee in the second person — withheld water and bread, web:Job.22.7 (תַּשְׁקֶ֑ה/תִּֽמְנַֽע, both 2ms) — interrupted at Job.22.8 by a third-person observation with no 2ms form anywhere in it, וְאִ֣ישׁ זְ֭רוֹעַ ל֣וֹ הָאָ֑רֶץ וּנְשׂ֥וּא פָ֝נִ֗ים יֵ֣שֶׁב בָּֽהּ (“But as for the mighty man, he had the earth. The honorable man, he lived in it.” web:Job.22.8), before the 2ms accusatory chain resumes at web:Job.22.9 (widows sent away empty, שִׁלַּ֣חְתָּ, 2ms; orphans' arms broken), before the unit closes with an explicit consequence particle, עַל כֵּ֭ן (oshb:Job.22.10, “Therefore snares are around you” web:Job.22.10), running through the floods-of-water image at Job.22.11. The whole span reads as one grounds-to-result movement: alleged sins, then their supposed effect on the accused.
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating Job.22.6-Job.22.11 as a mere continuation of the preceding questions rather than its own row was set aside, because the consequence particle at Job.22.10 closes a self-contained list-then-result unit that the interrogative series before it does not share.
next_row.literature_type_guess: Indictment catalog Job's concrete social-injustice accusations
